types.oie_definition: A human being, typically an individual with a name.
types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being, typically an individual with a name. Also called individual, human, person.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: All mentions are individual human names matching schema.org Person definition

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

types.oie_definition: A structured group of people with a particular purpose.
types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose. Also called institution, group, society.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: Mention is a structured group with a specific name matching schema.org Organization definition

mentions: International Union of Bakers and Confectioners (UIBC)

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

types.oie_definition: A prize given for excellence in a particular field.
types.embedding_query_text: Award: A prize given for excellence in a particular field. Also called honor, recognition, prize.

chosen_type.label: ConfectionerAward
chosen_type.definition: A prize awarded for excellence in the confectionery field
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org award type matches confectionery awards; minting specific type

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

types.oie_definition: A specific point in time expressed as a day, month, and year.
types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific point in time expressed as a day, month, and year. Also called day, calendar date, specific day.

chosen_type.label: RelativeDate
chosen_type.definition: A date expressed as a relative time period rather than an absolute calendar date
chosen_type.justification: Mentions 'last month' and 'July 14' don't match schema.org Date's absolute format

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.oie_definition: A large and permanent human settlement.
types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and permanent human settlement. Also called urban area, municipality, town.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: Singapore is a specific city matching schema.org City definition

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

types.oie_definition: A large, defined area with a common characteristic or boundary.
types.embedding_query_text: Region: A large, defined area with a common characteristic or boundary. Also called area, territory, zone.

chosen_type.label: DefinedRegion
chosen_type.justification: Brittany and Loire Valley are non-administrative defined regions matching schema.org DefinedRegion

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

types.oie_definition: A building or place where a particular activity is carried out.
types.embedding_query_text: Establishment: A building or place where a particular activity is carried out. Also called business, enterprise, venue.

chosen_type.label: LocalBusiness
chosen_type.justification: Both mentions are specific commercial establishments serving local communities

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Restaurant
candidates.comment: A Restaurant is a FoodEstablishment and LocalBusiness serving food and drink. Also called eatery, diner, cafe. Examples: "The French Laundry", a local pizzeria, a fast-food restaurant, a fine dining establishment.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

types.oie_definition: A well-known structure or feature that serves as a point of reference.
types.embedding_query_text: Landmark: A well-known structure or feature that serves as a point of reference. Also called monument, site, attraction.

chosen_type.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
chosen_type.justification: Château de Chambord is a historical landmark matching schema.org LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: TouristInformationCenter
candidates.comment: A local business providing information and services to tourists. Also called visitor center, tourist office, travel information point. Examples: a city visitor center, a national park information booth, a regional tourism office.

types.oie_definition: A sweet course typically served at the end of a meal.
types.embedding_query_text: Dessert: A sweet course typically served at the end of a meal. Also called sweet, confection, treat.

chosen_type.label: DessertItem
chosen_type.definition: A specific sweet course served at the end of a meal
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are specific dessert types not covered by existing schema.org FoodEstablishment subclasses

candidates.label: CafeOrCoffeeShop
candidates.comment: A CafeOrCoffeeShop is a FoodEstablishment primarily serving coffee, other beverages, and often light meals or pastries. Also called coffee house, coffee bar, cafe. Examples: Starbucks, local independent coffee shop, a small bistro. Distinct from Restaurant, which typically offers a wider range of full meals.

candidates.label: FoodService
candidates.comment: A FoodService is a Service related to providing food, such as breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Also called meal service, catering service, dining option. Examples: Breakfast service at a hotel, a school lunch program, an in-flight meal service, a catering package for an event.

candidates.label: FoodEvent
candidates.comment: A FoodEvent is an Event centered around food and drink. Also called culinary event, gastronomic event, food festival. Examples: A wine tasting, a cooking class, a food fair, a restaurant week promotion.

candidates.label: Bakery
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that bakes and sells bread, cakes, and pastries. Also called bake shop, patisserie, bread shop. Examples: "The Daily Bread Bakery", "Sweet Delights Patisserie", "Grandma's Oven".

candidates.label: Restaurant
candidates.comment: A Restaurant is a FoodEstablishment and LocalBusiness serving food and drink. Also called eatery, diner, cafe. Examples: "The French Laundry", a local pizzeria, a fast-food restaurant, a fine dining establishment.

types.oie_definition: A component used in the preparation of a dish or product.
types.embedding_query_text: Ingredient: A component used in the preparation of a dish or product. Also called component, element, additive.

chosen_type.label: SeaSalt
chosen_type.definition: A salt harvested from seawater, used as a culinary ingredient
chosen_type.justification: Salish salt is a specific type of salt not covered by existing schema.org ingredient types

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

types.oie_definition: A period of 365 days as a unit of time.
types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 days as a unit of time. Also called calendar year, annum, 12-month period.

chosen_type.label: Year
chosen_type.definition: A period of 365 days as a unit of time
chosen_type.justification: Mention '2012' represents a specific year not covered by existing schema.org duration types

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.
